subject: Dedicated multi-region capacity — pricing & commit options
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@datawave.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Dedicated multi-region capacity pricing and DR options

Hi Marissa / Rishi,

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a multi-region deployment and need detailed pricing and packaging options before our procurement review mid-March. High-level asks:
- Pricing bands for reserved commits (monthly/annual) for Dedicated GPU pools (NVIDIA H100-equivalent)
- Guidance on sizing per-region pools vs. a shared cross-region routing setup
- Incremental cost for active replication / hot-standby (DR) between US and EU pools
- Throughput guarantees (qps/token/sec) tied to commit levels and SLA credits

Expected traffic profile (very rough): 10M tokens/day steady-state, with 3x bursts during peak business hours; split roughly 70% US, 30% EU. We need a model that keeps tail latency <150ms for interactive use and supports predictable throughput for batch scoring jobs.

Can you share a proposal and any example pricing scenarios (3 region sizes: small/medium/large) and the assumptions behind throughput guarantees? Also, what discounts are available for 12/24-month committed spends?

Attaching our basic traffic profile.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform
DataWave Analytics
Attachments: DataWave_traffic_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@datawave.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated multi-region capacity pricing and DR options

Hi Alex — thanks for the context and the traffic profile. Quick acknowledgement: we can absolutely support a multi-region Dedicated deployment with per-region pools and a cross-region routing policy. A few clarifying questions so we size recommendations correctly:

- Are interactive requests latency-sensitive across both regions, or would you prefer routing interactive users to their local pool with background batch in a central region?
- Are there hard RTO/RPO targets for DR (e.g., sub-1hr RTO, near-zero token loss)?
- Do you plan to use the same model family/version across regions or have region-specific variants (quantized vs. FP16)?

Attached is a preliminary pricing proposal that outlines 3 example pool sizes (small/medium/large), committed monthly spend levels, and the baseline throughput we guarantee per pool. The proposal includes estimated discounts for 12- and 24-month commits and an optional replication add-on for active hot-standby across regions.

Summary highlights from the attached:
- Baseline: Dedicated pool unit = 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (small), scales in 4-GPU blocks
- Throughput SLO (medium pool): 250 tokens/sec sustained; tail latency <150ms for interactive under typical request sizes (<=1024 tokens)
- Replication add-on: 20-30% of committed cost for active replication (sync KV cache + periodic prefilling) depending on multi-region cross-traffic
- Discount bands: 10% (12mo), 18% (24mo) off list Dedicated rate; additional volume/strategic discounts available by exec approval

If that aligns, I'll prepare a more granular breakdown (per-region pool sizing, per-GPU throughput assumptions, and a recommended commit level for your 10M tokens/day profile).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing-proposal.pdf
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@datawave.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datawave.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Dedicated multi-region capacity pricing and DR options

Marissa, thanks — the deck looks useful. To answer your questions:

- Interactive traffic should stay local (US/EU) for end-user latency. We do expect cross-region failover so active sessions can be resumed if a region goes down (RTO target: 30–60 minutes).
- Near-zero token loss is preferred but not mandatory; we can accept a short warm-up window for cache population.
- We'll standardize on the same model family across regions; EU may run a quantized variant to reduce cost, but functional parity is required.

On pricing/discounts: given our ARR expectations for the next 12 months (~$1.2M consumption on inference), we're targeting a committed discount in the mid-20s (23–28%) if we sign a 24-month reserved commit that includes cross-region replication and a 24/7 support SLA. Can Redwood accommodate that level of discount and still meet throughput guarantees? Please confirm whether replication is priced as a % of committed cost (as in your deck) or per-GPU/replica.

Also, procurement will need: a sample doc showing latency SLAs, credit calculations, and an example Statement of Work for multi-region rollout.

Thanks — Alex

Attachments: DataWave_traffic_profile.xlsx (updated)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: Dedicated multi-region capacity pricing and DR options

Internal notes / ask: Alex (DataWave) is pushing for a 24-month commit with mid-20s discount (23–28%) and wants replication included. Traffic split ~70% US / 30% EU; target RTO 30–60m. They expect ~10M tokens/day (3x peaks).

Suggested commercial model to propose back:
- Commit baseline: 4 x large pools (US primary x2, EU primary x1, buffer pool for batch) sized as: US 2x medium pools (8 GPUs each), EU 1x medium pool (8 GPUs), burst buffer 1x small (4 GPUs) — total 28 GPUs reserved.
- Pricing: list rate for that config ~ $X/month; propose 22% enterprise discount on 24mo commit as standard, with room to move to 25% for legal-approved case (exec-signed credit).
- Replication: bill as 25% of committed monthly cost when active replication enabled (covers continuous KV cache sync, periodic prefill, and cross-region egress). This is simpler than per-GPU and easier to communicate to procurement.
- SLA credits: include a 99.9% regional availability SLA with credits scale; commit discount floors below which we require legal approval.

Questions for Rishi / Laura: are we comfortable with the 25% replication add-on and moving from 22 -> 25% if we need to close? Also confirm voucher/credit authority thresholds for offering an extra 2–3% (and whether Michael should handle escalation).

-- Marissa

Hi Alex — appreciate the clarity and the updated traffic sheet. We've reviewed internally and can put forward a commercial offer that aligns with your operational needs and procurement constraints. Summary below; full proposal attached and I included a DocuSign link to accelerate the paperwork.

Offer summary (DW-2026-014):
- Architecture: Per-region Dedicated pools (US primary: 2x medium pools = 16 GPUs reserved; EU primary: 1x medium pool = 8 GPUs reserved; burst buffer small = 4 GPUs). Total reserved: 28 GPUs (scales in 4-GPU blocks).
- Throughput SLOs: For the proposed config we guarantee 250 tokens/sec sustained per medium pool, with median latency <80ms and 95th percentile latency <150ms for requests <=1024 tokens. SLA: 99.9% regional availability; credits apply per the SLA grid in the attached SOW.
- Replication / DR: Active replication add-on priced at 25% of committed monthly cost (covers active-hot standby, KV cache sync, and prefill automation). Provides RTO target of <=60 minutes for session resumption and warm caches; near-zero token loss not guaranteed but we provide prioritized cache refill and traffic steering.
- Commercials: List rate for the above configuration is $X/month. Proposed committed discount: 24-month reserved commit at 25% off list. This includes the replication add-on in the committed price (no separate per-GPU charge).
- Support: 24/7 enterprise support included for the duration of the commit.
- Next steps: sign the attached MSA addendum and SOW (DocuSign link below). Once signed, we'll schedule a kickoff and a two-week prefilling window before go-live.
